The 90-Day
TRU Alpha Pilot
90-day-pilot-framework.subtitle: Test the journey. Understand the delivery. Make a clearer decision.
90-day-pilot-framework.label: Multi-site pilot framework

pages.title: Define the pilot
pages.intro: Start with one primary use case and representative clubs. Agree the evidence required before the first measurement.

rows: Retention, PT, performance or premium member experience
2–5 clubs reflecting relevant member, staffing and operational differences
Who is eligible, how they are invited and the intended sample
Baseline and, where feasible, a suitable comparison cohort or club
A defined operational or early commercial measure
Named sponsor, local owners and evaluation lead

blocks.text: A 90-day pilot can test adoption, operational fit and early coaching conversion. It cannot by itself establish an improvement in annual churn. Plan longer follow-up and an appropriate comparison for retention.

pages.title: Days 1–30: prepare and launch
pages.intro: Make the operating model consistent enough to understand differences between sites.

rows: Agree the use case, scope, site selection and primary question
Capture baseline, comparison approach and agreed metric definitions
Set decision criteria, expected sample and responsibilities
Train staff, confirm device guidance and support ownership
Prepare appointments, member messaging and reporting
Launch and check the first member journeys

blocks.text: Record eligible members, existing assessment and review activity, PT consultations and conversion where relevant, member feedback, staffing capacity and any concurrent promotions.
Key seasonal or commercial changes to account for

pages.title: Days 31–90: run, learn and evaluate
pages.intro: Use short operational reviews to resolve delivery issues without changing the evaluation question halfway through.

rows: Observe invitation, booking and first assessments

Updated uptake, return rates and capacity
Consistent site-level results and cost observations
Compare with baseline / suitable comparison and review economics

blocks.text: Review bookings, completions, missed appointments, staff cover, support issues and member feedback. Record any changes to the process and when they occurred.
Account for differences in member mix, staffing, promotions and seasonality. Self-selecting participants may differ from other members. Describe these limits when interpreting changes.

Plan retention follow-up over a suitable longer period, for example 6–12 months where appropriate to the business question. Agree comparable cohorts and an evaluation method before drawing conclusions.

pages.title: Build the cost picture
pages.intro: Use actual quotes and observed delivery time. Separate one-off investment, recurring cost and any revenue the operator actually receives.

blocks.text: Do not automatically add retained-member fees to acquisition savings. If departed members would have been replaced, account for replacement revenue and timing. Freelance PT package sales are not automatically club revenue.
